card.name: Words just before disease progression
card.fires_on: Small words like until, without, who had, or the word weight, where the next word likely to come is progression or progress. Mostly in oncology dosing lines and the phrase 'poor feeding and poor weight gain'.

modes.label: Until disease progression
modes.description: The word until or without in treatment-duration phrases, right before 'disease progression'.
modes.example: 360 mg every 3 weeks In combination with nivolumab until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or up to 2 years in patients<< without>> disease progression.

modes.label: Poor weight gain
modes.description: The word weight in infant-sedation warnings, after 'poor feeding and poor'.
modes.example: There are reports of sedation, poor feeding and poor<< weight>> gain in infants exposed to benzodiaz

modes.label: Patient status linking words
modes.description: Words like has or had after 'patient' or 'who' in course-repeat or prior-therapy conditions.
modes.example: consecutive days This five-day course may be repeated every 4 weeks for 2 courses, then every 4 to 5 weeks, if the patient<< has>> recovered from toxicity from the prior course.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward saying progress, progression or progressed as the next word.
card.plain: It fires on the small word just before 'disease progression' in treatment-duration wording.
